note: Replaces prior baseline.json. Total authenticated requests corrected from the prior report's 1,100 to the actual measured 2,000. Total across all benchmark gates (health/readiness + authenticated + worker): 5,100 successes, 0 failures, 0 timeouts.

1_health.description: High-concurrency health endpoint (/health) — no DB access, no auth, no rate limit
1_health.summary: 3,000/3,000 requests at c50 and c100, 0 errors, 0 timeouts.

2_readiness.description: Readiness probe (/ready) — executes async DB pool validation (SELECT 1)
2_readiness.summary: /ready is the bottleneck among public endpoints: pool acquisition + SELECT 1 yields p50 ~146ms@50 -> 238ms@100. 2,000/2,000 at c100. RPS peaks ~408 then drops to ~381 (saturation).

3_authenticated.description: Authenticated CRUD on 4 endpoints: GET /auth/me, GET /organizations, GET /orgs/:id/workspaces, GET /orgs/:id/projects. Bearer token (dev-only). GET-only, no rate limit.

4_database.summary: All EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) queries <0.4 ms, 99.65% cache hit ratio, index-scanned throughout.

5_pool.summary: PGPOOL_MAX=10 throughout. Never exceeded at c25/50/100. Saturation at c100: RPS 408->381, p50 /ready 238ms with sub-ms DB. Bottleneck = pool acquisition, not DB.

cpu.interpretation: Not compute-bound. Latency is wait-bound (I/O + pool acquisition).

apiWS.interpretation: V8 retains heap (~37MB growth under 4000 sustained c25 requests); no leak — growth bounded, Postgres flat. No OS-level return.

observationGaps: No V8 heap profiling — RSS used as proxy

bottleneckClassification.primaryBottleneck: Connection pool (PGPOOL_MAX=10) saturates at concurrency >10 for DB-backed endpoints. p50 /ready = 146ms@50 -> 238ms@100 despite sub-ms DB queries (0.3ms).
bottleneckClassification.secondaryBottleneck: No HTTP keepalive in harness — per-request TCP handshake adds latency.
bottleneckClassification.noCpuBottleneck: ~48% CPU during c25 burst, not compute-bound.
bottleneckClassification.noMemoryBottleneck: Bounded RSS growth, Postgres flat, no leaks.
